term: complete cause of an object's existence
definition: Under Rutten's interpretation G.edge c e means c brings e into existence as its complete cause. Several partial contributors jointly form one sum-cause, rather than each being that complete cause. The source separately requires one INCOMING complete cause per effect; it permits one cause to have many effects.
note: Graph.edge is still mathematically primitive: the name certifies no real causal role. Ordinary production suggests the interpretation, but no independently established physical example of the ENTIRE atomicity/complete-cause/nonoverlap/fusion profile is supplied here; the two-object model is only formal. Complete production differs from constitutive parthood, partial enabling contribution, temporal precedence and generic grounds. Nonoverlap/activity/unique-cause are separate policies, not laws inserted into Graph. No causal transitivity or WF is assumed. In particular R⊆Ground does not lift an uncaused R-source into a grounding root; Ground⊆R, contingent-R-causation or another faithful dictionary would need independent defense.
